candidates.tagline: Apple builds the touchscreen MacBook Jobs called 'ergonomically terrible'
candidates.story: On October 19, 2026 Apple confirmed its 'Pro and Tell' event launching the first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro — doing exactly what Steve Jobs said in 2010 'doesn't work' and is 'ergonomically terrible,' predicting users would get 'gorilla arm' from holding their arm up to poke a vertical screen.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent 16 years insisting touchscreen laptops are bad ergonomics and would tire your arm out, then built one anyway and named the launch event 'Pro and Tell.'
candidates.alt: A MacBook Pro laptop with a touchscreen display being tapped with a finger — the exact gorilla-arm ergonomic scenario Steve Jobs warned about in 2010

candidates.tagline: Third AI listening pendant this year raises $33M — investors haven't met Friend
candidates.story: On October 22, 2026, startup Nirva Labs raised $33 million for a $249 pendant that silently records only the wearer — the same concept as the widely-mocked Friend AI necklace (whose subway ads were vandalized with 'AI wouldn't care if you lived or died') and the discontinued Humane AI Pin, both of which flopped spectacularly.
candidates.why_funny: After Friend's New York subway ads were defaced and Humane's AI Pin was sold for parts, investors just handed $33M to the exact same always-on AI listening necklace idea in a prettier jewelry case.
candidates.alt: The Nirva AI pendant — a small silver and black jewelry pendant worn as a necklace that passively records everything its wearer says
